title: devops-g1-slo-dashboard
description: Uptime, SLI, error budget, burn rate, latency and saturation for POS. Every query mirrors an alarm in infra/observability.tf so a panel and its alarm cannot disagree. AUTHORED AS JSON -- not an export until re-exported from the workspace after it has been imported and each panel confirmed to render live data.

panels.title: Uptime — last 5m
panels.description: Mean of the canary's SuccessPercent over the window. The canary runs from outside the VPC (infra/observability.tf), which every in-VPC health check misses by construction.

panels.title: Uptime — last 1h
panels.description: Mean of the canary's SuccessPercent over the window. The canary runs from outside the VPC (infra/observability.tf), which every in-VPC health check misses by construction.

panels.title: Uptime — last 28d
panels.description: Mean of the canary's SuccessPercent over the window. The canary runs from outside the VPC (infra/observability.tf), which every in-VPC health check misses by construction.

panels.title: Uptime — latest minute
panels.description: SLO target for reference: ≥ 99.9% (docs/slo-error-budgets.md). Green ≥ 99.9, orange ≥ 99, red below.

panels.title: Canary success over time
panels.description: Same series as the stats above, at 1-minute resolution.

panels.title: POS SLI — pos_sale_write_total (namespace TillFlow, dimension OTelLib)
POS sale writes by result
panels.description: One series per result value: ok / idempotent / unique_violation are the SLI numerator, error is the failure half. A series exists only once it has been emitted, so 'error' is absent until the first failure.

panels.title: POS sale-write error rate
panels.description: bad / total, the same math as the burn-rate alarms (infra/observability.tf). Red line = 0.1%, the whole error budget as a rate. Reads 0 when no error series exists.

panels.title: POS error budget — target 99.9% over 28 days
Error budget remaining (28d)
panels.description: 100 × (1 − consumed). Consumed = failed writes ÷ (0.1% × eligible writes), summed over the 28-day window at daily resolution. Policy (docs/slo-error-budgets.md): below 25% → release freeze on pos; the freeze lifts above 50%. CloudWatch caps an alarm window at 7 days, so this panel is where the literal 28-day figure lives.

panels.title: Error budget remaining — 28d trend
panels.description: Same calculation as the stat, as a running series. Falls only when failed writes occur.

panels.title: Fast burn — page when BOTH windows exceed 14.4×
panels.description: Burn rate = error rate ÷ 0.1% budget. Multi-window (docs/slo-error-budgets.md): the 1h and 5m windows must both exceed 14.4× to page — the same pair infra/observability.tf alarms on.

panels.title: Slow burn — ticket when BOTH windows exceed 6×
panels.description: 6h and 30m windows must both exceed 6× to open a ticket — the same pair the slow-burn alarm uses.

panels.title: Latency and saturation — the same series the alarms watch
POS target latency p95
panels.description: AWS/ApplicationELB TargetResponseTime p95 for the pos target group. SLO: p95 < 400 ms (red line).

panels.title: POS ECS CPU / memory
panels.description: AWS/ECS utilisation for devops-g1-pos. Saturation gates from the k6 model: CPU < 70%, memory < 75% (the alarm thresholds).

panels.title: sale-events queue age
panels.description: AWS/SQS ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage for devops-g1-sale-events. Alarm threshold 120s (red line). The worker-down drill drives this (evidence/reliability-ops/g4-worker-down-drill.md).
